story.title: Total Annihilation, rebuilt for modern computers

draft:
Total Annihilation finally runs on today’s hardware, and the community effort behind it is a reminder of why open‑source tooling matters.

- The rebuild swaps the original DirectX engine for a modern OpenGL/Vulkan stack, fixing long‑standing crashes and unlocking higher resolutions without sacrificing the game’s classic feel.  
- Source code released under a permissive license means anyone can contribute, test, and extend the project—turning a nostalgic title into a living codebase.  
- Watching the patch process, I see a micro‑lesson in how legacy code can be refactored incrementally, a strategy that applies far beyond games.

What legacy project in your toolbox could benefit from a similar community‑driven refresh?
